summary: Exact crossing-surface conductor criterion, mixed-characteristic failures and a normal-component surface classification.
detailedSummary: For surface branches glued along a marked DVR, raw envelopes equal component envelopes away from the conductor and the minimum conductor value at the identified point; a greatest minorant exists exactly when those values agree. Positive gluing is proved with primary truncation. Explicit failures extend to mixed characteristic and every dimension. Universal CE for excellent surfaces with normal irreducible components is equivalent to zero-dimensional pairwise intersections.
text:
Consider R=k[x,y,z]_(x,y,z)/(xy) over any field, or R=V[[x,y]]/(xy) for a complete DVR V, with gauges m=(x,y,z) or(x,y,pi). In the latter case splitting formal series proves the fibre product V[[x]] times_V V[[y]], normalization product V[[x]] times V[[y]], and conductor(x,y). Both normalization factors are regular excellent normal surfaces. Their two conductor-boundary points map to one o. G331 supplies the full quotient and positive C/D descent.

For ANY finite continuous signed target obstacle f, let f_i be its component restrictions and H_i their greatest continuous geometric envelopes, existing by n1's arbitrary-characteristic normal-surface theorem. Let o_i be the conductor point and a=min(H_1(o_1),H_2(o_2)). Then the ENTIRE raw C/D supremum equals H_i(w) at every component point with finite w(x_i), and equals a at o, where x_1=x,x_2=y. A greatest C/D minorant exists precisely when H_1(o_1)=H_2(o_2); then the envelope is continuous and belongs to geometric C. Otherwise it is not USC and neither greatest minorant exists.

Here is the constructive lower bound with positivity. G331's normal zero dichotomy implies H_i(o_i)=0 only when H_i is identically0. If a=0 both envelopes are0 and p=0. If a<0, put B_i=(a/H_i(o_i))H_i when H_i(o_i)<0, and B_i=constant a when H_i=0. Then B_i is geometric C, B_i<=H_i<=f_i, and B_i(o_i)=a. For n>=1 define G_(i,n)=max(B_i,H_i-w(x_i)/n), taking the second term bottom when x_i is killed. Choose integer N>=n||H_i-B_i||. On the normalized section,
G_(i,n)=max(B_i,H_i-(1/n)w((x_i)+m_i^N)).
Indeed w((x_i)+m_i^N)=min(w(x_i),N), and H_i-N/n<=B_i everywhere. The right side belongs to C by granted addition, scaling and maxima, with an ACTUAL negative effective ample primary presentation for the ideal term. Thus G_(i,n) is continuous and positive in the geometric completed sense, equals a at the conductor and lies below f_i. The compatible tuple descends WITH POSITIVITY by G331, increases to H_i at finite-x_i points and retains a at o. This proves the raw lower bound. Every target D competitor pulls back to a source D minorant, hence is<=H_i and its common conductor value is<=both H_i(o_i). This proves the upper bound on ALL supports. No fibrewise minimum is silently treated as psh.

If conductor values match, the tuple H_i descends to the greatest continuous envelope. If H_1(o_1)>a, polynomial monomial w_r(x)=r,w_r(z)=1 tends on every element to o_1. In the DVR case define w_r(sum a_jx^j)=min_j(ord_pi(a_j)+rj), w_r(pi)=1. The associated graded domain proves multiplicativity, units have value0, and the values tend to ord_pi(a_0), or infinity if a_0=0. Continuity of H_1 yields p(w_r) tending to H_1(o_1)>p(o), contradicting USC of a greatest minorant.

The same criterion holds for finite q>=2 at an EXCELLENT local fibre product of excellent regular local SURFACE rings with surjective maps to the SAME marked DVR, nonzero principal kernels(x_i), and their product as finite normalization. The gauge must extend to primary gauges on every factor; all quotient points use the same quotient gauge. Take a=min_i H_i(o_i), use the same B_i and primary truncations with (x_i)+a_i^N, and require equality of ALL conductor values. At an incompatible value, G331 divisorial density supplies a convergent NET in the finite-kernel-value locus. These assumptions hold for k[x_1,...,x_q,z]_0/(x_ix_j:i!=j) and V[[x_1,...,x_q]]/(x_ix_j:i!=j), by separated-term expansion. No higher-dimensional conductor minimum field is claimed geometric.

The explicit proposed and signed model obstacles of n2 also work on V[[x,y]]/(xy), replacing z by pi. Generic branch2 order is min_j(ord_pi(a_j)+j). A generator attaining conductor order e has a nonzero pi^e coefficient in its y=0 residue, hence generic order<=e. Every arbitrary-support normalized valuation dominates ordinary m-order. The identical comparison, actual positivity and canonical ideals prove no greatest C/D minorant, with every-degree error1/2. This is a nonnormal mixed-characteristic failure, while the mixed cusp in n1 remains a CE example.

For EVERY d>=2 and field k the obstruction extends to R_d=k[x,y,z_1,...,z_(d-1)]_0/(xy). The conductor quotient is the z-ring, retaining ALL its supports. Set f=-1/2 on component1 and-1/2-1/(2w(y)) on component2, and F=(1/2)v((y)+m^2)-(3/2)v(m). They agree on the ENTIRE infinite-conductor stratum. Generic branch2 ordinary order and a conductor point with z_1=1, killing the other z_j, give the same ideal inequality. All branch2 points, including every conductor point, dominate generic order, so every minorant there is<=-1. The same h_n reach-1/2 at every finite-x first-component point. Thus p=-1/2 on that locus and-1 otherwise. In every degree,
A_m=(z_1,...,z_(d-1))^m+x(x,z_1,...,z_(d-1))^(ceil(m/2)-1)+y(y,z_1,...,z_(d-1))^(m-1).
The same component-order proof establishes this identity. Replacing t by min_j v(z_j) gives the same profile formula, pointwise convergence and exact uniform error1/2. Monomial rays x=r, all z_j=1 converge on every polynomial and local unit denominator to a conductor semivaluation. No higher-dimensional source CE theorem is used for these failures.

There is a sharp universal surface criterion. Let R be excellent reduced local of dimension at most TWO with NORMAL irreducible component rings R/p_i. Then ALL finite continuous signed obstacles have continuous geometric C/D envelopes iff dim R/(p_i+p_j)=0 for every distinct pair. Necessity is n3, already with signed primary models. For sufficiency S=product R/p_i is finite normalization. A support strictly below m cannot contain two minimal primes, since their sum has radical m. Its unique component quotient fixes its entire lift, and within a normal component normalization is the identity. Hence the FULL boundary map is bijective. G331 positive order/isometric descent and n1's normal-surface, DVR and empty cases give CE downstairs. On the punctured base only one normal component is present, so S/R is supported at the closed point. The conductor contains a power of m; it is unit in the normal case and proper primary in the genuinely nonnormal case. This classification does not cover irreducible nonnormal germs or arbitrary higher dimension.

More generally, whenever source CE holds at a finite normalization, constancy of the source envelope on EVERY target fibre is sufficient for continuous positive descent and equality of envelopes: every target competitor pulls back below it, and G331 descends the compatible envelope. Necessity is asserted only in the proved surface/DVR gluing sector. Homogeneous primary transport changes the component values by the same positive conductor denominator, preserving the criterion and raw formulas. Curve min(f,0), radial distinctions, all supports, nilpotent reduction and empty boundaries remain unchanged. Artifacts: n4.md and n4.tex. Rerun: python diagnostics.py; python deliver.py; python check_delivery.py. These are complete scoped draft deductions, not entire original closure.
